entities.summary: Choricius of Gaza was a prominent philosopher and thinker of the Classical era, who played a significant role in shaping the intellectual landscape of the ancient world. Born in the city of Gaza, in the Roman province of Syria, Choricius of Gaza was a key figure in the development of Neoplatonism, a philosophical school that emphasized the attainment of spiritual enlightenment through the study of Plato's works. His teachings had a lasting impact on the intellectual history of the Mediterranean world, influencing prominent thinkers such as Plotinus and Porphyry. Choricius of Gaza's philosophical ideas were characterized by their emphasis on the nature of the soul, the role of reason in achieving spiritual enlightenment, and the importance of the study of Plato's works. Through his writings and teachings, Choricius of Gaza helped to establish Gaza as a major center of learning and intellectual inquiry in the ancient world. His legacy continued to be felt for centuries, with many prominent thinkers drawing on his ideas and building upon his philosophical framework.
